meta.description: Covers: World Capitals & Currencies, Nobel Prizes & Awards, Literature, Geography, International Organizations, Pakistan Studies (Pre & Post Independence), General Science, Sports & World History — combined from multiple KU GK compilations and past-paper test banks

questions.question: Q1. Nobel Prizes are not given for which of the following field?
questions.explanation: The Nobel Prize categories are Physics, Chemistry, Physiology/Medicine, Literature, Peace, and Economic Sciences — there's no Music category.

questions.question: Q2. Men from which nation has won the highest number of Nobel Prizes?
questions.explanation: American laureates (from institutions and individuals) have collectively won more Nobel Prizes than any other nation, largely due to its strong research universities.

questions.question: Q3. Oscar award is related to:
questions.explanation: The Academy Awards (Oscars) honor achievement in the film industry, covering acting, directing, and technical filmmaking categories.

questions.question: Q4. Only Pakistani to receive an Oscar Award is _______.
questions.explanation: Sharmeen Obaid-Chinoy won Best Documentary Short twice (2012, 2016), making her the only Pakistani Oscar recipient.

questions.question: Q5. The Nobel peace prize is awarded in which city?
questions.explanation: Per Alfred Nobel's will, the Peace Prize is awarded in Oslo, Norway, while the other Nobel Prizes are awarded in Stockholm, Sweden.

questions.question: Q6. How many Pakistanis have won Nobel Prizes till now?
questions.explanation: Dr. Abdus Salam (Physics, 1979) and Malala Yousafzai (Peace, 2014) are the two Pakistani Nobel laureates to date.

questions.question: Q7. Who was the first Pakistani to win the Nobel Prize?

options.text: C) Dr Abdus Salam (Grand Unification Theory)

questions.explanation: Dr. Abdus Salam won the Physics Nobel Prize in 1979 for his contribution to the electroweak unification theory, becoming Pakistan's first Nobel laureate.

questions.question: Q8. How many Pakistani soldiers have been awarded Nishan-e-Haider (Highest Military Award of Pakistan) till now?
questions.explanation: Pakistan has awarded the Nishan-e-Haider, its highest gallantry award, to 11 soldiers since independence.

questions.question: Q9. Who is the only Pakistani recipient of India's highest civilian award, Bharat Ratna?

options.text: C) Bacha Khan (Khan Abdul Ghaffar Khan)

questions.explanation: Bacha Khan (Khan Abdul Ghaffar Khan), the Pashtun independence activist, remains the only Pakistani to receive India's Bharat Ratna.

questions.question: Q10. Dr. Linus Carl Pauling is the only person to have won two Nobel prizes individually for:

options.text: A) Chemistry in 1954, Peace Prize in 1962
B) Peace Prize in 1954, Chemistry in 1962

questions.explanation: Linus Pauling remains the only person to win two unshared Nobel Prizes — Chemistry in 1954 for his work on chemical bonding, and the Peace Prize in 1962 for his anti-nuclear activism.

questions.question: Q11. Who was awarded the Nobel Prize both for Physics and for Chemistry?
questions.explanation: Marie Curie won the Physics Nobel in 1903 (radioactivity) and the Chemistry Nobel in 1911 (discovery of radium and polonium).

questions.question: Q12. Nobel Prize are distributed annually at:
questions.explanation: Stockholm, Sweden hosts the annual Nobel Prize ceremony for Physics, Chemistry, Medicine, Literature, and Economics.

questions.question: Q13. Which is India's highest civilian award?
questions.explanation: The Bharat Ratna is India's highest civilian award, given for exceptional service in any field.

questions.question: Q14. Leaning Tower of Pisa is in:
questions.explanation: The Leaning Tower of Pisa, famous for its unintended tilt, is located in Pisa, Italy.

questions.question: Q15. Shekel is a currency of ______.
questions.explanation: The Shekel (New Israeli Shekel) is the official currency of Israel.

questions.question: Q16. Babylon is a city in ______.
questions.explanation: Babylon, an ancient Mesopotamian city known for its hanging gardens legend, is located in modern-day Iraq.

questions.question: Q17. Capital of Bahamas is:
questions.explanation: Nassau is the capital and largest city of the Bahamas.

questions.question: Q18. Australia's capital is ______.
questions.explanation: Canberra, a planned city, was chosen as Australia's capital as a compromise between rival cities Sydney and Melbourne.

questions.question: Q19. What is the Currency of Japan?
questions.explanation: The Japanese Yen (¥) is Japan's official currency.

questions.question: Q20. ______ is the national currency of Russia.
questions.explanation: The Russian Ruble is the official currency of the Russian Federation.

questions.question: Q21. The capital of New Zealand is:
questions.explanation: Wellington is the capital of New Zealand, though Auckland is the country's largest city.

questions.question: Q22. Phnom Penh is the capital of which of the following country?
questions.explanation: Phnom Penh is the capital and largest city of Cambodia.

questions.question: Q23. Which is the capital of Tajikistan?
questions.explanation: Dushanbe, meaning 'Monday' in Persian, is the capital of Tajikistan.

questions.question: Q24. ______ is the national currency of France.
questions.explanation: The Franc was France's currency before it adopted the Euro in 1999 (fully replacing it in 2002).

questions.question: Q25. What is the national currency of Germany?
questions.explanation: Germany adopted the Euro as its official currency after previously using the Deutsche Mark.

questions.question: Q26. The national currency of Sri Lanka is ______.
questions.explanation: The Sri Lankan Rupee is the official currency of Sri Lanka.

questions.question: Q27. What is the national currency of South Korea?
questions.explanation: The South Korean Won is the official currency of South Korea.

questions.question: Q28. What is the capital of Paraguay?
questions.explanation: Asunción is the capital and largest city of Paraguay.

questions.question: Q29. The capital of Russia is:
questions.explanation: Moscow has been the capital of Russia since 1918 (following a brief period with St. Petersburg as capital).

questions.question: Q30. Kampala is the capital of:
questions.explanation: Kampala is the capital and largest city of Uganda.

questions.question: Q31. Oslo is the capital of which country?
questions.explanation: Oslo is the capital of Norway.

questions.question: Q32. Havana is the capital of
questions.explanation: Havana is the capital and largest city of Cuba.

questions.question: Q33. Sana'a is the capital of ______.
questions.explanation: Sana'a is the capital of Yemen.

questions.question: Q34. The monetary unit (currency) of Bangladesh is:
questions.explanation: The Bangladeshi Taka is the official currency of Bangladesh.

questions.question: Q35. The national currency of India is ______.
questions.explanation: The Indian Rupee (INR) is India's official currency.

questions.question: Q36. The national currency of the United States of America (USA) is ______.
questions.explanation: The US Dollar (USD) is the official currency of the United States.

questions.question: Q37. What is the national currency of the United Kingdom?
questions.explanation: Pound Sterling (GBP) is the official currency of the United Kingdom.

questions.question: Q38. The national currency of Australia is ______.
questions.explanation: The Australian Dollar is Australia's official currency.

questions.question: Q39. What is the national currency of South Africa?
questions.explanation: The South African Rand is the official currency of South Africa.

questions.question: Q40. What is the national currency of New Zealand?
questions.explanation: The New Zealand Dollar is the official currency of New Zealand.

questions.question: Q41. ______ is the national currency of Afghanistan.
questions.explanation: The Afghani is the official currency of Afghanistan.

questions.question: Q42. What is the national currency of Nepal?
questions.explanation: The Nepalese Rupee is the official currency of Nepal.

questions.question: Q43. What is the national currency of China?
questions.explanation: The Chinese Yuan (Renminbi) is China's official currency.

questions.question: Q44. The capital of Afghanistan is:
questions.explanation: Kabul is the capital and largest city of Afghanistan.

questions.question: Q45. The capital of Argentina is:
questions.explanation: Buenos Aires is the capital and largest city of Argentina.

questions.question: Q46. The capital of Austria is:
questions.explanation: Vienna is the capital of Austria.

questions.question: Q47. The capital of Azerbaijan is:
questions.explanation: Baku is the capital of Azerbaijan.

questions.question: Q48. The capital of Bahrain is:
questions.explanation: Manama is the capital of Bahrain.

questions.question: Q49. The capital of Bangladesh is:
questions.explanation: Dhaka is the capital and largest city of Bangladesh.

questions.question: Q50. The capital of Belgium is:
questions.explanation: Brussels is the capital of Belgium and also hosts EU and NATO headquarters.

questions.question: Q51. The capital of Brazil is:

options.text: D) Rio de Janeiro (City of Brazil)

questions.explanation: Brasília, a planned city, has been Brazil's capital since 1960, replacing Rio de Janeiro.

questions.question: Q52. The author of the book "Time Machine" is:
questions.explanation: H.G. Wells wrote 'The Time Machine' (1895), a foundational work of science fiction.

questions.question: Q53. "Animal Farm" was written by?
questions.explanation: George Orwell's 'Animal Farm' (1945) is a satirical allegory of the Russian Revolution and Soviet totalitarianism.

questions.question: Q54. "War and Peace" was written by?
questions.explanation: Leo Tolstoy's 'War and Peace' is an epic novel set during the Napoleonic Wars in Russia.

questions.question: Q55. Who wrote the book "Forty Rules of Love"?
questions.explanation: Elif Shafak's 'The Forty Rules of Love' interweaves the story of Rumi and Shams of Tabriz with a modern narrative.

questions.question: Q56. "The Wealth of Nations" was written by?
questions.explanation: Adam Smith, often called the father of modern economics, wrote 'The Wealth of Nations' (1776).

questions.question: Q57. A famous novel "Pride and Prejudice" is written by;
questions.explanation: Jane Austen's 'Pride and Prejudice' (1813) is a classic novel of manners centered on Elizabeth Bennet and Mr. Darcy.

questions.question: Q58. Who has written the book "India Wins Freedom"?
questions.explanation: Maulana Abul Kalam Azad wrote 'India Wins Freedom', an account of the independence movement and partition.

questions.question: Q59. The book "Gulliver's Travels" was written by;
questions.explanation: Jonathan Swift wrote 'Gulliver's Travels' (1726), a satirical adventure novel.

questions.question: Q60. Who wrote the book "The Prince"?
questions.explanation: Niccolò Machiavelli wrote 'The Prince', a political treatise on power and statecraft.

questions.question: Q61. The book "Conquest of Happiness" was written by;
questions.explanation: Bertrand Russell wrote 'The Conquest of Happiness' (1930), a philosophical essay on achieving personal happiness.

questions.question: Q62. The celebrated novel "The Godfather" was authored by:
questions.explanation: Mario Puzo wrote 'The Godfather' (1969), later adapted into the acclaimed film trilogy.

questions.question: Q63. 'Zulfi, My friend' it is a book written by
questions.explanation: Piloo Modi wrote 'Zulfi, My Friend', a memoir about his friendship with Zulfikar Ali Bhutto.

questions.question: Q64. Who is the author of the book "1984"?
questions.explanation: George Orwell's dystopian novel '1984' (1949) depicts a totalitarian surveillance state.

questions.question: Q65. The book "The God of Small Things" is written by;
questions.explanation: Arundhati Roy won the Booker Prize for 'The God of Small Things' (1997).

questions.question: Q66. Who is the author of the book 'Satanic Verses'?
questions.explanation: Salman Rushdie wrote 'The Satanic Verses' (1988), a novel that generated major controversy in the Muslim world.

questions.question: Q67. Who wrote the line 'A thing of beauty is a joy forever'?
questions.explanation: John Keats opens his poem 'Endymion' with the line 'A thing of beauty is a joy forever.'

questions.question: Q68. The first history book was written by:
questions.explanation: Herodotus, a Greek writer, is widely regarded as the author of the first systematic history book, 'The Histories.'

questions.question: Q69. The famous book 'Anna Karenina' written by?
questions.explanation: Leo Tolstoy wrote 'Anna Karenina' (1877), a tragic novel of love and Russian aristocratic society.

questions.question: Q70. The height of Godwin Austin (K-2) is ______ meter.
questions.explanation: K2 (Godwin Austen), the world's second-highest peak, stands at 8,611 meters.

questions.question: Q71. The largest ocean in the world is
questions.explanation: The Pacific Ocean is the largest and deepest of the world's oceans.

questions.question: Q72. Harappa is situated near ______ in Pakistan.
questions.explanation: Harappa, one of the major Indus Valley Civilization sites, is located near Sahiwal in Punjab, Pakistan.

questions.question: Q73. Etna is a volcano in ______.
questions.explanation: Mount Etna, one of the world's most active volcanoes, is located in Sicily, Italy.

questions.question: Q74. Which lake is the largest in the world?
questions.explanation: The Caspian Sea, though called a 'sea', is the largest inland body of water (lake) in the world.

questions.question: Q75. Which country is known as the "Land of the Midnight Sun"?
questions.explanation: Norway is called the 'Land of the Midnight Sun' due to continuous daylight during summer in its northern regions.

questions.question: Q76. Which of the following is the biggest Island?
questions.explanation: Greenland is the world's largest island (Australia is classified as a continent, not an island).

questions.question: Q77. The Suez Canal joins the Mediterranean Sea with?
questions.explanation: The Suez Canal connects the Mediterranean Sea with the Red Sea, enabling shorter maritime trade routes.

questions.question: Q78. Farthest planet from the Sun:
questions.explanation: Neptune is the farthest planet from the Sun since Pluto was reclassified as a dwarf planet.

questions.question: Q79. River Thames is in which country?
questions.explanation: The River Thames flows through southern England, including London.

questions.question: Q80. Where is the Suez canal?
questions.explanation: The Suez Canal, connecting the Mediterranean and Red Seas, is located in Egypt.

questions.question: Q81. Which of the following is the largest of the Earth's oceanic divisions?
questions.explanation: The Pacific Ocean is the largest of Earth's oceanic divisions by area and volume.

questions.question: Q82. World's largest irrigation system is in ______.
questions.explanation: Pakistan's Indus Basin Irrigation System is considered the world's largest contiguous irrigation network.

questions.question: Q83. Which International Line separates Russia and Poland?
questions.explanation: The Curzon Line, proposed after WWI, was later used as a rough basis for the Poland–Soviet Union (Russia) border.

questions.question: Q84. Which is the largest desert in the world?
questions.explanation: By area, Antarctica (~14.2 million km²) is the world's largest desert — deserts are defined by low precipitation, not heat. The Sahara (~9.2 million km²) is only the largest HOT desert.

questions.question: Q85. Name the longest river in the world?
questions.explanation: The Nile River, flowing through northeastern Africa, is traditionally considered the longest river in the world.

questions.question: Q86. Which is the deepest ocean in the world
questions.explanation: The Pacific Ocean's Mariana Trench is the deepest point in any ocean on Earth.

questions.question: Q87. What is the radius of earth?
questions.explanation: Earth's mean radius is approximately 6,371 kilometers.

questions.question: Q88. The Second largest continent in the World is
questions.explanation: Africa is the second-largest continent by both area and population, after Asia.

questions.question: Q89. The "River Mackenzie" is located in:
questions.explanation: The Mackenzie River, Canada's longest river, flows through the Northwest Territories into the Arctic Ocean.

questions.question: Q90. The largest latitude circle on earth is:
questions.explanation: The Equator is the largest circle of latitude, dividing Earth into Northern and Southern Hemispheres.

questions.question: Q91. Victoria desert is in
questions.explanation: The Victoria Desert is located in Australia, spanning South Australia and Western Australia.

questions.question: Q92. Which is the largest Gulf in the world:
questions.explanation: The Gulf of Mexico is the largest gulf in the world by area.

questions.question: Q93. Suez canal separates African continent from:
questions.explanation: The Suez Canal separates the African continent from Asia at the Sinai Peninsula.

questions.question: Q94. The bridge in Istanbul which connects Asia and Europe is called:
questions.explanation: The Bosporus Bridge (now 15 July Martyrs Bridge) spans the Bosporus Strait, connecting Europe and Asia in Istanbul.

questions.question: Q95. ______ has the world's largest natural gas reserves.
questions.explanation: Russia holds the world's largest proven natural gas reserves.

questions.question: Q96. International Court of Justice is headquartered in
questions.explanation: The International Court of Justice (ICJ), the UN's principal judicial organ, is headquartered in The Hague, Netherlands.

questions.question: Q97. The headquarters of the United Nations (UN) is located at:
questions.explanation: The United Nations headquarters is located in New York City, USA.

questions.question: Q98. How many members are there in European Union?
questions.explanation: The European Union currently has 27 member states following the UK's exit (Brexit) in 2020.

questions.question: Q99. The largest stock exchange in the world is:
questions.explanation: The New York Stock Exchange (NYSE) is the world's largest stock exchange by market capitalization.

questions.question: Q100. NATO stands for
questions.explanation: NATO stands for the North Atlantic Treaty Organisation, a military alliance founded in 1949.

questions.question: Q101. Pakistan is not a member of:
questions.explanation: Pakistan is a member of the OIC, ECO, and NAM, but not the G-8 (now G-7 plus Russia's former inclusion).

questions.question: Q102. Headquarters of Economic Cooperation Organization (ECO) is at:
questions.explanation: The Economic Cooperation Organization (ECO), which includes Pakistan, Iran, and Turkey among others, is headquartered in Tehran, Iran.

questions.question: Q103. World Bank headquarters are at ______.
questions.explanation: The World Bank is headquartered in Washington, D.C., USA.

questions.question: Q104. The countries that are part of NAFTA are
questions.explanation: NAFTA (now replaced by USMCA) was a trade agreement between the USA, Mexico, and Canada.

questions.question: Q105. Which of the following is not a G-7 country?
questions.explanation: The G-7 comprises Canada, France, Germany, Italy, Japan, the UK, and the USA — Russia is not currently part of it.

questions.question: Q106. Which of the following is not an agency of the UN:
questions.explanation: ASEAN (Association of Southeast Asian Nations) is a regional bloc, not a specialized agency of the United Nations.

questions.question: Q107. Interpol headquarters are at
questions.explanation: Interpol, the international police organization, is headquartered in Lyon, France.

questions.question: Q108. Which of the following is a Military Alliance?
questions.explanation: NATO is a military alliance formed to provide collective defense among its member states.

questions.question: Q109. Headquarters of ILO (International Labour Organisation)
questions.explanation: The International Labour Organization (ILO) is headquartered in Geneva, Switzerland.

questions.question: Q110. Which of the following is not chief organ of the United Nations Organizations?
questions.explanation: The UN's six principal (chief) organs are the General Assembly, Security Council, ECOSOC, Trusteeship Council, ICJ, and Secretariat — the OIC is a separate intergovernmental body.

questions.question: Q111. Amnesty International works for:

options.text: A) Peace between India and Pakistan

questions.explanation: Amnesty International is a global NGO focused on documenting and campaigning for human rights.

questions.question: Q112. G-7 is a group of
questions.explanation: The G-7 is a forum of the world's seven largest advanced economies.

questions.question: Q113. WHO is headquartered in:
questions.explanation: The World Health Organization (WHO) is headquartered in Geneva, Switzerland.

questions.question: Q114. Albert Einstein was a famous:
questions.explanation: Albert Einstein was a theoretical physicist best known for the theory of relativity.

questions.question: Q115. Who is also known as the lady with the lamp?
questions.explanation: Florence Nightingale, a pioneer of modern nursing, earned the nickname 'The Lady with the Lamp' during the Crimean War.

questions.question: Q116. Qutbuddin Aibak is the founder of which ruling era?
questions.explanation: Qutbuddin Aibak founded the Slave (Mamluk) dynasty, the first dynasty of the Delhi Sultanate.

questions.question: Q117. Who invented Penicillin?
questions.explanation: Alexander Fleming discovered penicillin in 1928, revolutionizing the treatment of bacterial infections.

questions.question: Q118. Who invented the light bulb?
questions.explanation: Thomas Edison is widely credited with inventing the practical incandescent light bulb.

questions.question: Q119. Daily Dawn was founded by
questions.explanation: Dawn was founded by Quaid-e-Azam Muhammad Ali Jinnah in Delhi on 26 October 1941 as the mouthpiece of the All-India Muslim League.

questions.question: Q120. Who was the first ruler of the Mughal dynasty?
questions.explanation: Babur founded the Mughal dynasty in India after defeating Ibrahim Lodi in 1526.

questions.question: Q121. Who made Pakistan's flag?
questions.explanation: Ameer-ud-Din Qudwai is credited with designing Pakistan's national flag.

questions.question: Q122. Taj Mahal was built by?
questions.explanation: The Taj Mahal was built by Mughal Emperor Shah Jahan as a mausoleum for his wife Mumtaz Mahal.

questions.question: Q123. Who is the president of Syria?
questions.explanation: Bashar al-Assad has served as President of Syria since 2000.

questions.question: Q124. Who is the PM of Israel?
questions.explanation: Benjamin Netanyahu has served multiple terms as Prime Minister of Israel.

questions.question: Q125. Who is the father of Geometry?
questions.explanation: Euclid, an ancient Greek mathematician, is known as the 'Father of Geometry' for his work 'Elements.'

questions.question: Q126. The youngest certified Microsoft technology specialist is:
questions.explanation: Arfa Karim Randhawa became the world's youngest Microsoft Certified Professional at age 9.

questions.question: Q127. The first man to set foot on the Moon was ______.
questions.explanation: Neil Armstrong became the first person to walk on the Moon during the Apollo 11 mission in 1969.

questions.question: Q128. Who built the Eiffel Tower?
questions.explanation: Gustave Eiffel's engineering firm designed and built the Eiffel Tower for the 1889 Paris World's Fair.

questions.question: Q129. Michael Jackson is a distinguished person in the field of?
questions.explanation: Michael Jackson, known as the 'King of Pop,' was one of the most influential figures in pop music.

questions.question: Q130. Mount Everest was ascended in 1953 by:
questions.explanation: Edmund Hillary and Tenzing Norgay together made the first confirmed ascent of Mount Everest in 1953.

questions.question: Q131. Leonardo da Vinci:

options.text: A) Was a great Italian painter, sculptor and architect
B) Got universal fame from his masterpiece "Monalisa"
C) Drew models of organs such as the heart, lungs and womb

questions.explanation: Leonardo da Vinci was a true Renaissance polymath — painter, sculptor, architect, and anatomist, famous for the Mona Lisa.

questions.question: Q132. Neil Armstrong and Edwin Aldrin were the first to
questions.explanation: Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin became the first humans to step on the Moon's surface in 1969.

questions.question: Q133. The Law of Natural Selection is associated with
questions.explanation: Charles Darwin proposed the theory of natural selection as the mechanism driving evolution.

questions.question: Q134. George Bernard Shaw, the great dramatist, was
questions.explanation: George Bernard Shaw, the celebrated playwright and Nobel laureate in Literature, was Irish.

questions.question: Q135. Euclid was

options.text: B) Contributor to the use of deductive principles of logic as the basis of geometry

questions.explanation: Euclid systematized geometry through deductive logic in his work 'Elements,' laying foundations still used today.

questions.question: Q136. Where was Jesus Christ born?
questions.explanation: According to the Bible, Jesus Christ was born in Bethlehem, near Jerusalem in Judea.

questions.question: Q137. September 11, 1948 - Which of the following events was marked on this day?
questions.explanation: Muhammad Ali Jinnah, founder of Pakistan, passed away on September 11, 1948.

questions.question: Q138. Liaqat Ali Khan was assassinated in Rawalpindi on ---
questions.explanation: Liaquat Ali Khan, Pakistan's first Prime Minister, was assassinated in Rawalpindi on October 16, 1951.

questions.question: Q139. Prince ______, Duke of Edinburgh, died at age of 99 on 9 April 2021?
questions.explanation: Prince Philip, Duke of Edinburgh and husband of Queen Elizabeth II, died on 9 April 2021 at age 99.

questions.question: Q140. When was the first Pakistani constitution drafted?
questions.explanation: Pakistan's first constitution was drafted and adopted in 1956.

questions.question: Q141. Gwadar became part of Pakistan on
questions.explanation: Gwadar was purchased from the Sultanate of Oman and became part of Pakistan on September 8, 1958.

questions.question: Q142. In which of the following year Pakistan accepted Bangladesh as an Independent country.
questions.explanation: Pakistan formally recognized Bangladesh as an independent state in 1974.

questions.question: Q143. Second constitution was passed in
questions.explanation: Pakistan's second constitution was promulgated by President Ayub Khan in 1962.

questions.question: Q144. Objective Resolution was passed in?
questions.explanation: The Objectives Resolution, laying the ideological foundation for Pakistan's constitution, was passed in 1949.

questions.question: Q145. Simla agreement was signed in the year?
questions.explanation: The Simla Agreement between Pakistan and India was signed in 1972 following the 1971 war.

questions.question: Q146. Who was the youngest Nishan-e-Haider of Pakistan?
questions.explanation: Rashid Minhas, a PAF pilot who died in 1971, is the youngest recipient of the Nishan-e-Haider.

questions.question: Q147. Which pass connects Pakistan with Afghanistan?
questions.explanation: The Khyber Pass, through the Spin Ghar mountains, is the main historic route connecting Pakistan and Afghanistan.

questions.question: Q148. In which year Pakistan became nuclear power?
questions.explanation: Pakistan conducted its nuclear tests and became a declared nuclear power in 1998.

questions.question: Q149. The first constructed barrage of Pakistan is
questions.explanation: The Sukkur Barrage, completed in 1932, was Pakistan's (British India's) first major barrage on the Indus.

questions.question: Q150. Pakistan Steel mill founded with the help and cooperation of
questions.explanation: China provided significant assistance in establishing the Pakistan Steel Mills in Karachi.

questions.question: Q151. Gwadar Port is constructed in the province of
questions.explanation: Gwadar Port, a deep-sea port and key CPEC project, is located in Balochistan.

questions.question: Q152. One of the founders of Indian National Congress was
questions.explanation: Allan Octavian Hume, a British civil servant, was a key founder of the Indian National Congress in 1885.

questions.question: Q153. Liaqat Ali Khan was born in
questions.explanation: Liaquat Ali Khan was born in Karnal, in present-day Haryana, India.

questions.question: Q154. Who Presented Lahore Resolution (Pakistan Resolution) on 23rd March, 1940?

options.text: C) Quaid e Azam Muhammad Ali Jinnah

questions.explanation: The Lahore Resolution (Pakistan Resolution) was moved by A.K. Fazlul Haq, with Quaid-e-Azam Muhammad Ali Jinnah presiding over the 1940 session.

questions.question: Q155. The gas predominantly responsible for global warming is
questions.explanation: Carbon dioxide, released mainly from burning fossil fuels, is the primary greenhouse gas driving global warming.

questions.question: Q156. Electric current is measured by
questions.explanation: An ammeter is the instrument used to measure electric current in a circuit.

questions.question: Q157. The dynamo is the device for converting:

options.text: A) Heat energy into electrical energy
B) Mechanical energy into electrical energy
C) Magnetic energy into electrical energy

questions.explanation: A dynamo (generator) converts mechanical energy into electrical energy through electromagnetic induction.

questions.question: Q158. The hardest substance available on earth is:
questions.explanation: Diamond, a crystalline form of carbon, is the hardest naturally occurring substance.

questions.question: Q159. Washing soda is the common name for:
questions.explanation: Washing soda is the common name for sodium carbonate (Na₂CO₃).

questions.question: Q160. Which of the following order is given to the planets of solar system on the basis of their sizes:
questions.explanation: By size, the order from largest is Jupiter, Saturn, Earth, then Mercury (the smallest planet).

questions.question: Q161. The solar eclipse occurs when:

options.text: A) The sun comes between the moon and the earth
B) The earth comes in between the sun and the moon
C) The moon comes in between the sun and the earth

questions.explanation: A solar eclipse occurs when the Moon passes between the Sun and Earth, blocking sunlight.

questions.question: Q162. Who invented the telephone?
questions.explanation: Alexander Graham Bell is credited with inventing and patenting the first practical telephone in 1876.

questions.question: Q163. What is the boiling temperature of water?
questions.explanation: Water boils at 100°C (212°F) at standard atmospheric pressure.

questions.question: Q164. Which of these is not a mosquito borne disease:
questions.explanation: Goitre is caused by iodine deficiency, not mosquito transmission — unlike dengue, malaria, and filariasis.

questions.question: Q165. Oranges are a rich source of:
questions.explanation: Oranges are well known as a rich source of Vitamin C.

questions.question: Q166. Which acid is produced when milk gets sour?
questions.explanation: Lactic acid is produced by bacteria fermenting lactose when milk turns sour.

questions.question: Q167. People with which blood group are called universal donors?
questions.explanation: People with blood group O (specifically O-negative) are considered universal donors since their red cells lack A/B antigens.

questions.question: Q168. Thermometer is related to degree in the same way as clock is related to:
questions.explanation: Just as a thermometer measures degrees, a clock measures hours — both are instruments for measuring their respective units.

questions.question: Q169. Which instrument is used to measure pressure?
questions.explanation: A manometer is used to measure the pressure of gases and liquids.

questions.question: Q170. The unit of current is
